3dc347e9217687c6.h:
Valentine's Day (United States)

1847 to 1881
Esther Howland (New England Valentine Company)

A folded card of paper lace, a ribbon, a verse for someone you love. Esther Howland of Worcester, Massachusetts, received an English valentine in 1847 and set out to make her own. Her brother took samples on a sales trip, hoping for $200 in orders, and came back with $5,000. She set the women working for her along a table, each adding one part of the card, and checked every one herself. Her valentines went out across the country, and sales grew to $100,000 a year.

d4df028c46e48763.h:
Easter

1875 on
Cadbury

The egg hunt in the garden, the basket, the purple foil. Fry's of Bristol moulded the first hollow chocolate Easter eggs in 1873, but the chocolate egg took off two years later, when Cadbury began making them: dark chocolate, filled with sugared almonds. Cadbury turned to milk chocolate eggs in 1905, took in Fry's in 1919, and launched the Creme Egg in 1971. It now makes about 500 million Creme Eggs a year.

ef7adad4d4c4bbd9.h:
Halloween (trick-or-treating)

1950s on
US candy makers

Children in costumes walking the street at dusk, pillowcases getting heavier. Early trick-or-treaters were given cookies, fruit, nuts, coins or toys; Halloween was not a candy holiday until the 1950s, when the big candy makers began running Halloween promotions. Later they wanted the walk to happen in daylight, so children would have an extra hour to collect candy. At the 1985 Senate hearings on daylight saving time, the industry put candy pumpkins on every senator's seat, as Michael Downing, author of a history of daylight saving, told NPR. In 2005 Congress moved the end of daylight saving to the first Sunday in November, just late enough to include Halloween night.

From the record

Group
Corporatized a holiday
Holiday
Halloween (trick-or-treating)
The record
Halloween was not a candy holiday until the 1950s, when big candy manufacturers began putting out many more Halloween promotions, and wrapped candy became the usual treat. Later the industry wanted trick-or-treating covered by daylight saving time so children would have an extra hour to collect candy; at the 1985 Senate hearings on daylight saving it put candy pumpkins on every senator's seat. In 2005 daylight saving was extended to the first Sunday in November, just long enough to include Halloween.

entries.title: Who corporatized holidays, by year
entries.note: Although usually originating authentically, holiday momentum has largely become economic in nature or at least numb under it, the occasions not collective memories but commodification by commercial interests, their relationships almost entirely manufactured, no longer genuine celebration but consumption oftentimes suppressing the very qualities that they claim to honor. The companies and trade bodies behind it, listed by the year they began. Pick one to read its story. Compiled for the Culprits map from the sources in each story (Wikipedia, histories and reporting). Each point is placed where its record says.

Invented Arthur's Day in 2009 for Guinness's 250th anniversary, named after the brewery's founder: a yearly round of pub promotions and free music events in Ireland and 55 countries. Ireland's junior health minister called it a pseudo-national holiday invented for marketing; Dublin's ambulance service reported a 30 percent rise in call-outs one year. Guinness dropped it in 2014.

Small Business Saturday

2010 on
American Express

The weekend after Thanksgiving, and a sign in the corner shop window asking you to shop small. The day was invented by a credit card company. American Express created Small Business Saturday in 2010, the day after Black Friday. In 2011 the US Senate passed a resolution declaring it, and American Express holds the name as its registered trademark.

entries.title: 2014 · Chinese New Year (Spring Festival)
entries.html:
Chinese New Year (Spring Festival)

2014 on
Tencent (WeChat)

Red envelopes of money passed from elders to children at the New Year, a custom more than 500 years old. In 2014 Tencent put the red envelope inside WeChat, its messaging app, as a way to send money. WeChat users sent 16 million of them that year and about a billion the next. In 2015 Tencent paid China Central Television US$7.7 million to sponsor the New Year gala, the year's most watched broadcast, and viewers shook their phones on cue to win cash.

entries.kind: Mexico's tourism board and the James Bond film Spectre
entries.html:
Day of the Dead (Mexico City)

2016 on
Mexico's tourism board and the James Bond film Spectre

Families keeping vigil at the graves of their dead, talking and singing to them. Mexico City's huge Day of the Dead parade, with its giant skeletons and floats, is a recent addition. It was written for a film: the 2015 James Bond movie Spectre opened with an invented skeleton parade in the city. In 2016 the city staged a real one to match, and the government tourism board that sponsored it called it part of a campaign to bring tourists during the holiday.
